statisticsCandidate.strategy: GF-only exact aliases for the two repository specifiers to dedicated userscript/translationInsights.ts; keep shared runtime and all other outputs unchanged.

reachableConsumers.connectionTest: No repository import. Optional recordModelUsage callback is not provided by the GF platform; providers retain request observers without a database dependency.
reachableConsumers.visionProbe: visionProbeRuntime imports the same translateWithCache broker plus its independent visionProbeStorage. That supported storage is unchanged.
reachableConsumers.ReadingPanel: Imports reading client and sends runtime messages. It imports no statistics repository; GF platform exposes no model-usage/translation-stats dashboard/clear handler. Reading and feature UI are retained.

privacyAndGenerationProof: GF metadata contains only http://*/* and https://*/* @match.
isExtensionModelUsageRuntime compares location.protocol with chrome-extension:, moz-extension:, safari-web-extension:; all are false in the supported GF page scope.
Model usage capture already returns0 on HTTP(S); recordModelUsage returns before reading the repository.
Translation stats capture is unconditional in the original runtime. Repository generation starts at0; capture is a pure read; only clear() increments it.

The current graph has no external repository clear/getDashboard/getRequestLog/importData/exportData call or repository exposure; the only external references are the four broker callbacks. Thus the original GF translation stats generation remains0.
Original HTTP(S) recordTranslationRequest never calls repository.record; queue stays empty and no flush timer or statistics writes are scheduled.

protectedSupportedCode: SelectionTranslator, SettingsPanel, ReadingPanel, FloatingBall, ShareCardStudio and full-page/input/section translation are live product components; their size alone is not deletion evidence.

boundedConclusion: The two concrete reachability candidates address accidental retention without moving primary product logic to resources. Their combined existing code-span inventory is79046 bytes, before adapters/layout changes and without a candidate build. It is not a measured net saving, not proof of satisfying the349380-byte gap, and not a global Pareto/size limit. Pure data screening adds no such proof. Further work requires actual candidate builds and exact final artifact acceptance.
